name: Strait of Hormuz
description: Between Iran and Oman/UAE, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. Commercial shipping lanes are only about 2 miles wide in each direction at the narrowest crossing.
significance: Carried roughly 21 million barrels per day of petroleum liquids in 2022, about 21% of global petroleum liquids consumption -- the U.S. EIA calls it the world's most important oil transit chokepoint.
significance_source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) -- The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most important oil transit chokepoint

name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
coordinate_source_name: Wikipedia -- Strait of Bab al-Mandab (GeoHack coordinates)
description: Between Yemen (Arabian Peninsula) and Djibouti/Eritrea (Horn of Africa). Connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. Only 26km (14 nautical miles) wide at its narrowest point, limiting tanker traffic to two 2-mile-wide channels.
significance: One of only a few true global submarine-cable chokepoints: 14 cables ran through the Red Sea corridor it anchors as of 2024, with 6 more planned, carrying over 90% of Europe-Asia internet traffic. A February 2024 cable-cut incident here (AAE-1, EIG, Seacom, TGN-Gulf systems) knocked out roughly 25% of Red Sea cable capacity and caused documented outages in Djibouti and Bahrain.
significance_source_name: TeleGeography (via PBS/AP reporting) and HGC Global Communications

name: Suez Canal (northern end / Port Said)
description: Man-made canal in Egypt linking the Mediterranean Sea (Port Said) to the Red Sea (Suez), forming the northern anchor of the same Red Sea shipping corridor that Bab-el-Mandeb anchors to the south. Opened in 1869.
significance: Normally carries about 15% of global maritime trade volume -- the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe. Red Sea attacks cut Suez Canal transit volume by 50% year-over-year in the first two months of 2024, per the IMF's PortWatch platform, as shipping diverted around the Cape of Good Hope (adding 10+ days to voyages).
significance_source_name: International Monetary Fund -- 'Red Sea Attacks Disrupt Global Trade' (March 7 2024)
